subscription_products.product_name: Hill's Science Diet Puppy Large Breed Chicken & Brown Rice Recipe Dry Dog Food, 27.5-lb bag
subscription_products.subscription_rationale: Feeding math for Buddy (2-mo, 30 lb): large-breed puppies at this weight commonly need ~3 cups/day while growing. 1 cup dry kibble ≈ 4 oz (0.25 lb). A 27.5-lb bag contains ≈ 110 cups (27.5 lb ÷ 0.25 lb/cup = 110 cups). At 3 cups/day → 90 cups/month. 110 cups ÷ 90 cups/month ≈ 1.22 months per bag (≈5–6 weeks). Food is an everyday consumable during rapid growth — auto-ship avoids interruption and keeps Buddy on a consistent large-breed, beef-free diet.
subscription_products.personalized_note: Buddy is only 2 months and already 30 lb — Hill's large-breed puppy formula will give the right calories and controlled calcium/protein for steady growth. Set this on auto-ship so you never run out while puppy growth is fastest.

subscription_products.product_name: Pupford Chicken Soft & Chewy Training Dog Treats, 5-oz pouch
subscription_products.subscription_rationale: Training math for Buddy: puppies in early housetraining/socialization often use 8–12 small treats/day. Assume 10 treats/day at ~2 g each = ~20 g/day. 5-oz pouch ≈ 142 g. 142 g ÷ 20 g/day ≈ 7 days. For heavy short-term training, a weekly refill or bi-weekly larger shipment prevents interruption of positive reinforcement.
subscription_products.estimated_frequency: Every week (adjustable as training intensity changes)
subscription_products.personalized_note: Buddy will be doing a lot of quick rewards for crate and potty training — these small chicken treats are perfect, beef-free for his allergy risk. Auto-ship weekly now, then reduce frequency as training solidifies.

Disposable pads are a short-term consumable during Month 1–3 of housetraining; subscription prevents running out during this intense phase.
subscription_products.personalized_note: Buddy's apartment housetraining will be much easier with disposable potty pads on hand — stocking a monthly supply means fewer late-night runs to the store and fewer accidents while he learns.

One 24-count pack lasts ≈12 days, so ~2–3 packs/month are typical. Wipes are high-frequency consumables worth auto-shipping while Buddy is young and training indoors.
subscription_products.personalized_note: With Buddy being a Golden and you living in an apartment, quick paw and face wipes will keep your floors cleaner and make coming in from rainy walks less stressful — auto-ship keeps them on hand for daily use.

one_time_products.personalized_note: Buddy needs carefully measured portions to avoid too-rapid growth — this kitchen scale helps you feed exactly what his vet or feeding guidelines recommend. Buy once and use for months of accurate feeding.

overall_strategy: Cold-start Month 1 for a 2-month-old, 30-lb Golden Retriever living in an apartment: prioritize durable setup essentials (crate + divider, bowl, harness, cooling mat/bedding, raincoat, crate mat, stuffable chew toys, camera, scale) as one-time buys to keep Buddy safe and comfortable immediately. Simultaneously auto-ship high-frequency consumables that deplete quickly during intensive housetraining and early socialization: puppy kibble (large-breed formula), training treats, disposable potty pads, grooming/paw wipes, enzymatic cleaner, and calming-diffuser refills. I showed the math for consumption estimates (food cups per day, treat grams per day, pads per day, wipes usage) to justify cadence — start with slightly aggressive frequencies for the first 1–3 months while Buddy is being house-trained and socialized, then downshift subscription frequency as training stabilizes and consumption normalizes.
